original_question: Develop effective invariants and, if possible, a classification theory for welded knots. In particular, determine whether Satoh's map from welded knots or links to ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space is faithful, and determine whether a welded knot with trivial fundamental group must itself be trivial as a welded knot.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact core of the paper's official open problem: it asks for good invariants and possible classification of welded knots, asks whether Satoh's map to ribbon tori in four-space is faithful, and includes the companion question of whether trivial fundamental group forces a welded knot to be trivial.
missing_details: The paper's hidden definition of a welded knot should be made explicit: welded knots are the equivalence classes obtained from virtual knot diagrams by allowing the classical and virtual Reidemeister moves together with only one forbidden move, namely the upper forbidden move.
Satoh's construction is asked about on equivalence classes of welded knots (and links), not merely on chosen diagram representatives.
The codomain should be stated exactly as ambient-isotopy classes of embeddings of tori, specifically ribbon tori, in four-dimensional space.

The nearby context explains why these questions are singled out: Satoh's map is already known to induce an isomorphism from the welded knot's combinatorial fundamental group (indeed, its quandle) to the fundamental group of the complement of the associated ribbon torus.
The second question is specifically about welded knots, not links, and 'trivial' means trivial as a welded knot.

The paper's wording is 'construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, to classify them'; the draft's phrases 'effective invariants' and 'classification theory' are accurate in spirit but slightly broader than the official wording.
No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers are relevant here; the missing stand-alone details are topological definitions and the exact domain/codomain.
refined_question: Let a welded knot or link mean an equivalence class of virtual knot or link diagrams modulo the classical and virtual Reidemeister moves together with the upper forbidden move. Construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, classify them by deciding whether Satoh's map from equivalence classes of welded knots (respectively, welded links) to ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-dimensional space is faithful; in particular, does a welded knot with trivial combinatorial fundamental group have to be the trivial welded knot?
justification: The draft does not target Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; it clearly targets the open problem stated in Section 8.1, item 6, titled 'Welded knots'. The wording there is nearly verbatim to the draft: first the paper asks for good invariants and possible classification of welded knots, then it asks whether Satoh's mapping is faithful, and finally it asks whether trivial fundamental group implies welded triviality. The adjacent sentences provide the needed scope and hidden assumptions: welded knots are obtained by allowing only the upper forbidden move, and Satoh's map is already known to preserve the combinatorial fundamental group/quandle via an isomorphism with the complement group of the associated ribbon torus. This is a topological problem, so algebraic data such as base field, degree, homogeneity, or asymptotic quantifiers are not applicable. The paper does not explicitly prove any alternate equivalent reformulation of the problem, so no alternate formulation should be added.
